name: Refugee / Asylum Seeker Registration (UNHCR, Outside Domestic Law)

requirements.blocker_text: Afghanistan has no confirmed domestic legal or constitutional basis for asylum -- UNHCR's own Afghanistan help portal states foreigners seeking protection inside Afghanistan should email UNHCR with contact details and await follow-up, or register in person at the ICON Compound in Kabul (Mondays and Wednesdays, 8:30am-12:30pm). No refugee-status-determination procedure, timeline, or legal criteria are published; the only confirmed benefit of registration is that a UNHCR refugee/asylum-seeker certificate unlocks free care at designated public hospitals (with case-by-case help for private healthcare costs) plus access to referenced legal-assistance services. This is Afghanistan's version of the pattern seen elsewhere in this dataset (Algeria, Haiti, Cuba) where UNHCR runs protection entirely outside state law -- but thinner than any of those: Afghanistan is overwhelmingly a REFUGEE-PRODUCING country (2.6 million registered Afghan refugees worldwide per UNHCR), and no evidence was found of any non-Afghan refugee population or dedicated domestic government protection body operating inside the country.
requirements.fix_path: Email UNHCR Afghanistan with contact details, or register in person at the ICON Compound in Kabul during posted hours, to obtain a refugee/asylum-seeker certificate.

evidence_required.document: UNHCR registration email or in-person appointment record

sources.title: UNHCR Help Afghanistan -- registration process (email / ICON Compound Kabul walk-in hours) and healthcare access for refugees and asylum seekers inside Afghanistan

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Afghanistan). STATUS: DRAFT -- best sourcing reached tier 2 (UNHCR's own portal); no Afghan government body, decree, or constitutional asylum provision was found, and none is claimed to exist. GENUINE, SEVERE FINDING: this is the thinnest domestic-protection framework found in this dataset to date -- not merely 'no domestic law, UNHCR fills the gap' (as with Algeria, Haiti, Cuba), but a country that is itself the dominant SOURCE of refugees globally (2.6 million registered Afghan refugees worldwide, per UNHCR's own Afghanistan reporting), with no confirmed evidence that a parallel inbound-protection system for non-Afghans has any real operational depth beyond an email inbox and two weekly walk-in windows in Kabul. family_can_join set to false (schema requires a boolean) -- no derivative-family provision was found, not a confirmed denial. family_can_work left null and study_rights omitted (not a required field): not addressed by the source. work_rights set to 'none' since no work authorization was mentioned anywhere in the registration process description, only healthcare and legal-assistance access.
